title: aura_visual
summary: Benilla's aura-state CharProc layer changes how the unit's own BODY renders for the life of an aura: proc 14 translucency (Stealth 0.3, Invisibility/Fade 0.5, ghost, Shadowform, Banish) with the 1000 ms cubic ramp both ways, proc 1 body tint (Frostbolt chill blue, Immolate orange, poison green), proc 11 animation freeze (Ice Block holds the pose), plus display-row base alpha (Ghost Wolf's CreatureModelAlpha 102). MSUI parses SpellVisualKit CharProcs (Formats/SpellVisualCatalog.cs) but consumes ONLY the type-9 emitter proc; there is no code path applying alpha, tint, or an anim-rate freeze to a unit's model - a stealthed player renders fully opaque, Ice Block does not freeze the pose, no chill/poison tint ever shows.

openItems.text: Proc 14 translucency: no aura-driven body alpha at all (no stealth/invisibility/ghost fade; grep for stealth/translucency/CreatureModelAlpha in the render stack finds nothing).
Proc 1 tint: no aura-driven body color modulation.
Proc 11 anim-rate: no freeze of the unit's animation clocks under Ice Block/Petrify-family auras.
Base display alpha: CreatureDisplayInfo's CreatureModelAlpha is not applied, so authored-translucent displays (Ghost Wolf) render opaque.
